When deciding whether to fight a fire, there are several critical safety considerations that should be evaluated first:

A. "Am I safe from toxic smoke and gases?" - This is definitely important because toxic smoke and gases can quickly incapacitate someone or cause serious health issues.

B. "Do I have an escape route?" - This is crucial because if the fire grows or changes direction, you need to be able to exit safely.

C. "Do I have the right extinguisher?" - This is also important because different types of fires require different extinguishing agents.

All three of these considerations are important safety checks before attempting to fight a fire. In fire safety training, people are typically taught to first ensure their own safety (which includes protection from smoke/gases and having an escape route) before attempting to fight a fire, and then to make sure they have the appropriate equipment.
